what: The Running Pace Calculator links pace, time and distance. Give it any two and it works out the third, in kilometers or miles.
It also lists even splits for each kilometer or mile and predicts your times for common races using Riegel's formula, a well-known method used by runners and coaches.
uses: Find the pace you need for a target time.
Turn a time and distance into pace and speed.
See likely times for 5K to marathon from a recent race.
Get the time you should pass each km or mile.
tutorial: Click "Find pace", "Find time" or "Find distance". The box you are finding is greyed out.
Pick a race such as 5K or Marathon, or type a custom distance and choose kilometers, miles or meters.
Type minutes and seconds and choose per kilometer or per mile.
See pace per km and per mile, speed in km/h and mph, finish time and distance.
Read the even splits table and the race predictions table.
features: Split and running total for each km or mile.
Warns about world-record-fast or walking-slow paces.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A 10K in 50:00 is a pace of 5:00 per km (8:03 per mile) and a speed of 12 km/h. Riegel predicts about 23:59 for 5K, 1:50:19 for a half marathon and 3:50:01 for a marathon. Running a marathon at 5:00 per km takes 3:30:59.

tips: Use a recent race or hard time trial for predictions, not an easy run.
Longer predictions need matching long-run training.
Plan slightly slower first splits on race day to avoid fading.
Hills, heat and wind add time; adjust your goals.
problems: A message says the pace is faster than the world record
Check the units: you may have entered miles as kilometers or minutes as hours.
Very long distances show only the first 200 splits.
You are in "Find distance" mode. Click another mode to type a distance.
